disagreements.positions: agent_3 25.5x ($302 FV); agents 1 and 5 26x ($312 / $304); agent_2 27x ($319; SEMI shows growth continuing in 2028); agent_4 28x ($321; 12-24 month tool lead times give backlog visibility).
disagreements.resolution: Not settleable by search, and the range is narrow: on ~$12 NTM EPS, 25.5x vs 28x is $306 vs $336, only about 0.2 of a one-year sigma. Two base-rate facts bound it. (1) Lam's year-end trailing P/E fell in the year after each of the last three multiple peaks: 15.9x to 6.8x (2017-18), 21.3x to 11.0x (2021-22), 29.7x to 21.7x (2023-24). The 2024 de-rating (-27%) came in a year when WFE still grew, so growth continuing in 2028 does not by itself stop a de-rating. (2) Part of it has already happened: the June 30 high of $438.50 was ~46x FY27 consensus and today is ~34x FY27 / ~27.6x FY28. Peers sit at similar forward multiples (AMAT ~29x, KLAC ~36x), so this is a sector re-rating, not a Lam anomaly. On a rolling NTM basis (today ~32x NTM EPS of ~$10.1) the agents' 25.5-28x already assumes a 13-20% de-rate, which lines up with the milder of the historical cases. I centre on ~26x (fair value ~$312) and keep the deeper, 2018/2022-style de-rate in the left tail.
disagreements.evidence: CompaniesMarketCap year-end P/E history; StockAnalysis statistics for LRCX, AMAT and KLAC (Sep 30, 2026: LRCX forward P/E 34.2x, trailing 56x).

disagreements.topic: Is there an edge vs spot ($324.48)?
disagreements.positions: Every fair value is at or below spot ($302-321), yet the mean ladder puts P(>=324) at 0.502 (median ~$325). Agent_2 (FV $319, median ~$340) and agent_4 (FV $321, median ~$335) put their ladder medians $15-20 above their own fair values. Agents 1, 3 and 5 have medians within $3-18 of their fair values.
disagreements.resolution: No meaningful edge. The fair-value gap to spot is -1% to -7%, which is about 0.1 of a one-year sigma (~0.50) and roughly offset by the normal equity drift for a beta-1.9 stock. So the right answer is a ladder near a coin flip at spot, tilted slightly below 0.50 to match the agents' own central values. I set the median at ~$320 (P(>=324) = 0.490), about 1 pt below the mean. The right skew (scenario means $332-351) stays in the upper strikes.
disagreements.evidence: Agent files (fair_value vs reasoning medians); StockAnalysis beta 1.86.

disagreements.topic: Agent_4's 3.5% memory-spot haircut to FY28 EPS
disagreements.positions: agent_4 cuts FY28 consensus from $11.74 to $11.30 because DRAM/NAND spot prices cooled in September. The other four use consensus.
disagreements.resolution: Not supported. TrendForce's Sep 30 contract-price outlook, the price series that drives memory-maker capex, has conventional DRAM contracts +10-15% QoQ and NAND +15-20% in 4Q26, with server DRAM undersupplied and PC DRAM tight into 2027. Micron guided FY27 capex 'above the mid-$40 billion range' (June call). A soft patch in DDR4 spot is not a capex signal, so the haircut should go. It moves agent_4's P/E leg by only ~$12.

summary: Round 2 converged: all five now use the $9.51/$11.74 FY27/FY28 consensus and SEMI's +22%/+14% WFE path, and fair values sit in a tight $302-321 band against a $324.48 spot. The only remaining disagreement is the Sept-2027 multiple (25.5-28x NTM), and history says semicap de-rates after multiple peaks (Lam's year-end P/E fell 27-57% in 2018, 2022 and 2024). Treat it as a small, high-beta satellite and expect large swings around the late-October report.
